# chronosphere_notebook (Resource)

A Chronosphere notebook, a document of text, queries, and panels defined by `notebook_json` and owned by a collection. The API rejects edits from the Chronosphere app to a notebook that Terraform manages.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "chronosphere_collection" "c" {
  name = "Platform"
}

resource "chronosphere_notebook" "oncall_runbook" {
  name          = "On-call runbook"
  slug          = "on-call-runbook"
  collection_id = chronosphere_collection.c.id

  labels = {
    "team" = "platform"
  }

  notebook_json = jsonencode({
    version = 1
    document = {
      type = "doc"
      content = [
        {
          type    = "heading"
          attrs   = { level = 1 }
          content = [{ type = "text", text = "On-call runbook" }]
        },
        {
          type    = "paragraph"
          content = [{ type = "text", text = "Start with the service dashboard, then check recent deploys." }]
        },
      ]
    }
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `collection_id` (String) ID of the collection that owns this notebook. A collection's `id`, or `USER:<slug>` for a user's personal collection.
- `name` (String) Display name of the notebook. Can be changed after creation.
- `notebook_json` (String) JSON payload describing the notebook's content. Must be a JSON object. Wrap with `jsonencode({...})` in HCL. The provider compares canonical JSON, so key ordering and whitespace do not cause spurious plans.

### Optional

- `labels` (Map of String) Key/value labels attached to the notebook for organization and filtering.
- `slug` (String) Stable identifier for the notebook. Generated from `name` if omitted. Immutable after creation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
